newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian lead market seen flat - Cominco.
newsitem.headline: Asian lead market seen flat - Cominco.

text.p: The Asian lead market is likely be flat this year due to bumper supplies from China, Europe and the U.S. being sold in the region, a senior official at Canadian miner Cominco Ltd said on Tuesday.
"The glow is off lead," Colin Blyth, managing director of Asia Pacific Cominco Metals pte Ltd, said in an interview with Reuters.
"There's a lot of people offering lead," he said, citing specifically the large amounts of Chinese metal being exported, "even non-registered brands."
"All traditional western suppliers seemed to be saying we've got to move the tonnage and let's put a little bit more in Asia," Blyth added.
Average premiums for long-term lead contracts this year fell to US$120 a tonne over London Metal Exchange cash prices against $135 in 1996.
"We booked the same level of sales, but in order to do those sales the premium had to go down," Blyth said.

Cominco estimates western refined lead consumption will reach around 5.2 million tonnes this year versus production of about 5.1 million tonnes. Year-end stocks are projected at around 300,000 tonnes.
But these estimates do not include lead coming from non-traditional producers and this makes it difficult to gauge the whole supply picture, Blyth said.
"That can easily flip to a surplus," he said. "The reality is that you see more of this lead come out."
